findings.fact: The wrapper defaults to one upload worker and passes --jobs explicitly. Its 64-path batches are sequential, not 64 upload workers.

--build enumerates derivation requisites including outputs, omits .drv paths, and then sets --no-closure. Attic subsequently filters already cached and upstream-signed paths. Planned paths are not an actual-upload count.
Each client worker awaits one path upload before taking another. The CLI default 5 is overridden by the wrapper observed at 1.

Each chunked NAR request creates its own 10-permit semaphore. The receiver waits for a permit before spawning; the permit remains held through chunk upload and chunk-reference database insertion. This is not a process-wide upload cap.

The pinned server says its 10-chunk concurrency is not configurable. S3 files below 8MiB use one PutObject; multipart files spawn an upload task for each 8MiB part before join_all, with no separate part semaphore. Actual fanout depends on compressed chunk sizes, deduplication and concurrent clients.

Warm upload command failures/timeouts are recorded as warnings then exit 0. This does not make warming asynchronous: publish-index needs the completed build-platform matrix, including warming and log-artifact steps.

The failure-tolerant branch covers the wrapped upload command. Earlier test -n ATTIC_TOKEN/status-file setup and later summary/artifact failures are not covered by that branch and can still fail the job. The declared warm command budget is 30m plus 30s kill grace.

limits: No attribution of the Flink checkpoint delay or earlier native timeout to cache warming is established.
The InternalServerError client class does not identify the server/database/S3 cause.
No new concurrency limit, deadline, retries, cache deletion, workload cancellation or storage mutation was made.

options.status: Requires a separate exact-source closure handoff or rebuild/queue design. Merely detaching the process loses runner lifetime guarantees; a fresh warmer can duplicate work. Preserve both native gates, archive/source/platform verification, credential restrictions and the full intended cache closure before considering such restructuring.
